_: Mark surface geometry and gate tolerances. Read by src/lib/mark-scale.ts,
which derives display heights, and by scripts/check-marks.mjs, which gates
the rendered result. One file because two copies of a threshold drift, and
a gate whose threshold disagrees with the code it guards passes defects.
inkCap / inkFloor / maxInkWidth are CSS px, and they constrain the INK box,
not the image box: several assets carry 20-56% of their file as transparent
padding, which costs nothing to render and must not be charged against the
tolerance is NOT chosen. Each is the tightest band the current assets
actually satisfy, measured by `pnpm check:marks --sweep` and rounded up one
0.01 step for sub-pixel headroom. Improve an asset and it can tighten.

rail.note: Forced by two marks. Richemont at 14.45:1 sits on the 15px ink floor and still carries 12.6% more ink than the median; Chalhoub and Alshaya are near-square and hit the 68px cell ceiling 12.8% under it. The set needs a 5.16x ink-height range and the cell offers 4.53x. The floor stays at 15 because it is a legibility floor and lowering one to make a gate greener is the gate lying. Dropping it to 12px takes this surface to 0.0%, which is Sumeet's call.

card.note: The mark box grows from 24px to 32px, which is measured rather than aesthetic: at a 24px cap the five marks now on cards cannot come closer than 27.4% of their median, because the set needs a 3.18x range and 24 over a 10px floor gives 2.4x. Measured figure moved 0.004 to 0.005 when mark-scale.ts's tie-break started preferring the larger R of an equal-deviation plateau, same fix as axis below.

axis.note: Round 14, two changes. First, and the actual fix: mark-scale.ts's search kept the FIRST reference height R that hit the best deviation, which on this surface is the SMALLEST of a whole plateau (R=18 through 30 all land on 0.0000) rather than a single optimum — so it was rendering the smallest of many equally-correct sizes. Ties now keep the larger R, free size at no deviation cost: Microsoft went 14px to 24px, SAP 9px to 16px, with the gate's own number improving 0.008 to 0.003. Second, inkCap raised 26 to 34 for headroom once Blue Yonder and Informatica joined the set, though the chosen R lands inside the old ceiling too — the plateau was already there.

entity.note: A single mark on a case-study page. A set of one is its own median, so there is nothing to normalise against and the cap governs.
